entries.title: Exodus 3:1
segments: Horeb; a mountain in Arabia between the two arms of the Red sea.

entries.title: Exodus 3:2
segments: Flame of fire--bush; the manner of the vision was a striking symbol of the condition of Israel, burned in the furnace of persecutions, but not consumed.

entries.title: Exodus 3:5
segments:
Holy ground; to be treated with peculiar reverence, because of the manifestation of Jehovah there. 
 
The place where God manifests himself has a peculiar sanctity; and if we should approach him acceptably, it must be with reverence and godly fear. 
 
The comfort of our thanksgivings to God, the peace we have through faith in Christ, and the joy of communion with him and his people, we should ever remember are mercies which come to us through the Saviour's blood.

entries.title: Exodus 3:9
segments: Jehovah is a just, and also a kind, compassionate, and merciful God. He tenderly sympathizes with all the distressed, especially such as wrongfully suffer; and in due time he will deliver the oppressed, and punish the oppressor.

entries.title: Exodus 3:11
segments:
Who am I? expressing a sense of his insufficiency. 
 
The kindness and condescension of God, in communing with his people, and permitting them to feast with him on the riches of his grace, are unspeakably great.

entries.title: Exodus 3:12
segments:
This shall be a token; the fulfilment of this prediction would be to Moses and Israel a sign that God had sent him. 
 
However unworthy men may be, and however insufficient in themselves for services to which God calls them, if he grant them his presence they may fearlessly go forward, expecting to be crowned with success.

entries.title: Exodus 3:14
segments: I am that I am; either, I am he who I am; or, I am that which I am.  In either case, the words denote the self-existent, eternal, and incomprehensible nature of Jehovah.  As the only original Being, he is the ground of all created being. Compare

entries.title: Exodus 3:15
segments: The eternal, unchanging perfections of Jehovah are a proper ground for implicit confidence in him, and prompt, persevering obedience to all his commands.

entries.title: Exodus 3:16
segments: Elders of Israel; their head men.

entries.title: Exodus 3:18
segments: Met with us; appeared to us and given us directions.

entries.title: Exodus 3:19
segments: No, not by a mighty hand; not though I deal with him by a mighty hand.  He would withstand all God's mighty judgments, till the last great plague.

entries.title: Exodus 3:20
segments: Neither the power of God, nor the truth of his promises, nor the certainty that they will be accomplished, renders the use of means unnecessary, or furnishes any ground to expect his blessing in the neglect of them.

entries.title: Exodus 3:21
segments: Give this people favor; lead the Egyptians to furnish them the things they should ask for, and which they had doubtless earned.

entries.title: Exodus 3:22
segments: Borrow; the word rendered borrow, means also, to request or demand, not expecting to make a return.
Jewels; the word rendered jewels means also furniture, utensils, and goods of various descriptions.
Spoil the Egyptians; carry away the rich treasures which they shall give you.
